raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partially_feasible",
    "answerable": [
      "Day-of-year of snowmelt onset (SWE peak-to-decline / disappearance) at each of the 6 SNOTEL locations via independent single-column ELM runs",
      "Correlation of simulated and observed melt-onset DOY against station elevation",
      "Elevation-driven ordering/ranking of melt timing across the 6 stations against SNOTEL SWE observations"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "A physically-resolved LOCAL lapse rate BETWEEN stations from ELM alone: gridded atmospheric forcing (GSWP3/CRUNCEP ~0.5-1 deg) does not resolve inter-station (sub-12 km) temperature gradients; the apparent lapse rate is imposed by forcing downscaling, not simulated ridge microclimate",
      "Wind redistribution / preferential deposition of snow on ridges (not represented in column ELM)",
      "Aspect/slope radiation contrasts unless explicitly set per column"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "The request targets each individual SNOTEL station and the inter-station lapse rate, so one dedicated single-column ELM run is placed at each of the 6 Naches SNOTEL sites (no aggregation), enabling per-site melt-onset DOY and elevation regression.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "white_pass",     "lat": 46.611, "lon": -121.391, "soil_texture": "gravelly_sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "bumping_ridge",  "lat": 46.872, "lon": -121.309, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "morse_lake",     "lat": 46.571, "lon": -121.491, "soil_texture": "gravelly_loam"},
    {"id": "pigtail_peak",   "lat": 46.512, "lon": -121.444, "soil_texture": "gravelly_sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "cougar_mountain","lat": 46.851, "lon": -121.331, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "fish_lake",      "lat": 46.703, "lon": -121.204, "soil_texture": "loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "H2OSNO",
      "SNOW_DEPTH",
      "QMELT",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "FSNO",
      "SNOW",
      "RAIN",
      "TSA",
      "TG",
      "TSOI",
      "FSDS",
      "FIRA",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "single_column_ELM",
    "site_forcing_downscaling_with_elevation_correction",
    "SNOTEL_SWE_ingest_for_evaluation",
    "per_column_surface_dataset_generation"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "STOP_OPTION=nyears with a 20-year spin-up recycling 1980-2018 forcing before the 39-year evaluation run to equilibrate snowpack/soil states",
    "Each column uses its actual station elevation for atmospheric lapse-rate downscaling of temperature, pressure, humidity, and longwave (default T lapse ~6.5 K/km) so melt-timing differences are elevation-consistent",
    "Melt-onset DOY defined as the first day after peak SWE with a sustained SWE decline (e.g. >5 consecutive days negative dSWE), computed identically for model and SNOTEL",
    "Vegetation set to evergreen needleleaf boreal/temperate forest with grass understory typical of Cascade subalpine SNOTEL sites unless site metadata indicates open meadow",
    "Flat, all-sky column (no explicit aspect/slope) — aspect effects treated as a caveat, not resolved",
    "SNOTEL station coordinates/elevations approximate published NRCS metadata; verify against station catalog before run"
  ]
}

answerable: Day-of-year of snowmelt onset (SWE peak-to-decline / disappearance) at each of the 6 SNOTEL locations via independent single-column ELM runs
Correlation of simulated and observed melt-onset DOY against station elevation
Elevation-driven ordering/ranking of melt timing across the 6 stations against SNOTEL SWE observations
not_answerable: A physically-resolved LOCAL lapse rate BETWEEN stations from ELM alone: gridded atmospheric forcing (GSWP3/CRUNCEP ~0.5-1 deg) does not resolve inter-station (sub-12 km) temperature gradients; the apparent lapse rate is imposed by forcing downscaling, not simulated ridge microclimate
Wind redistribution / preferential deposition of snow on ridges (not represented in column ELM)
Aspect/slope radiation contrasts unless explicitly set per column

parsed.n_justification: The request targets each individual SNOTEL station and the inter-station lapse rate, so one dedicated single-column ELM run is placed at each of the 6 Naches SNOTEL sites (no aggregation), enabling per-site melt-onset DOY and elevation regression.
assumptions: STOP_OPTION=nyears with a 20-year spin-up recycling 1980-2018 forcing before the 39-year evaluation run to equilibrate snowpack/soil states

Each column uses its actual station elevation for atmospheric lapse-rate downscaling of temperature, pressure, humidity, and longwave (default T lapse ~6.5 K/km) so melt-timing differences are elevation-consistent
Melt-onset DOY defined as the first day after peak SWE with a sustained SWE decline (e.g. >5 consecutive days negative dSWE), computed identically for model and SNOTEL
Vegetation set to evergreen needleleaf boreal/temperate forest with grass understory typical of Cascade subalpine SNOTEL sites unless site metadata indicates open meadow
Flat, all-sky column (no explicit aspect/slope) — aspect effects treated as a caveat, not resolved
SNOTEL station coordinates/elevations approximate published NRCS metadata; verify against station catalog before run
